title: CSS That Computes, Layouts That Lerp, Type as Frames, Critters & a Code Field
description: A diffusion model in pure CSS, breakpoint-free interpolation, frame-played type, procedural critters and a spring-plate code input.

drops.title: A Model in the Stylesheet
drops.description: 601 typed @property registers, a seed frozen by a checkbox, and five unrolled denoise steps — with zero JavaScript.
drops.concept: diffusion.css runs a real denoising diffusion model in CSS alone, and the mechanism is the story: typed custom properties compute instead of expanding textually, a counting keyframe animation holds a live seed until :has(#go:checked) pauses it, mod() hashes that seed into noise, and because CSS has no loops every sampler step gets its own copy of the arithmetic. This drop is a miniature of that machine — a 10x10 grid, a 4-neighbour kernel on a schedule that blurs early and sharpens late — with the filmstrip showing each settled state.

interaction.mouse: Nothing to hover — the page has no scripts at all.
interaction.click: Press the button to freeze the animated seed; the whole chain settles on that sample.
interaction.touch: Same single control, sized for thumbs; uncheck to re-roll a new seed.

drops.title: Layout That Interpolates
drops.description: Drag a container wider and every value glides — columns, padding, weight, rotation, hue — with no breakpoint anywhere.
drops.concept: cq-lerp turns a container's own width into one unitless progress value and then writes every property as base + range x t. The hard part is that plain calc() cannot divide two lengths, so it leans on tan(atan2(a, b)) — which is exactly a/b — until the native progress() function ships. The third card puts @container breakpoints next to the interpolated version so you can watch one snap while the other glides.

interaction.mouse: Drag the green handle on any card to resize its container and watch t climb.
interaction.click: Switch between linear t and smoothstep easing; every rule re-reads the same number.
interaction.touch: Handles are pointer-event driven, and a width slider drives all three cards at once.

drops.title: Type That Is Played, Not Animated
drops.description: Six text animations that are just lists of frames with hold times — braille, blocks, rain and a parametric reveal.
drops.concept: thought-stream treats a text animation as a plugin: an array of frames, an interval, and an optional per-frame pause. The engine advances the list, redraws only the rows whose text changed, and pauses when the tab is hidden, the element scrolls away, or the visitor prefers reduced motion. Rows that get rewritten flash white here so you can see the diffing happen.

interaction.mouse: Drag the speed slider to stretch or compress every hold time at once.
interaction.click: Step frame-by-frame, or pause the whole page's engine from one button.
interaction.touch: Type into the text field to rebuild the parametric text_reveal plugin live.

drops.title: Creatures That Chase the Pointer
drops.description: A joint chain with a bend cap, feet that plant where they land, and grip that falls as they lift.
drops.concept: cursor-critters builds its motion out of a simulation rather than keyframes: each body joint eases toward the one ahead with a rate that decays down the chain, so the tail always lags; feet step in diagonal pairs and plant where they land; and acceleration is scaled by traction = 0.16 + planted/total x 0.84, which produces the crouch-push-glide rhythm. Three species here share one solver and differ only in their parameters.

interaction.mouse: Move over a tile and the critter chases the pointer, leaning into its turns.
interaction.click: Pointer-down anchors the target; the tuning panel rebuilds the body live.
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across a tile to lead it; let go and it wanders the box on its own.

drops.title: The Code Field That Merges
drops.description: A one-time-code input where a spring-driven plate slides between cells and a correct code melts the row into a pill.
drops.concept: modern-otp-input-v2 hides one real <input> under presentational cells, so paste, software keyboards and autocomplete="one-time-code" keep working while every pixel is custom. A spring (k 240, c 31) carries the focus plate to the active cell, digits fade up out of a 6px blur through the Web Animations API, a wrong code dissolves them right to left and counts the attempt, and a right one runs the row's geometry through data-phase states until it is a single Verified pill.

interaction.mouse: Click a row to focus it; the plate springs to the cell the caret is on.
interaction.click: Use the Mail suggestion chip to autofill, or type a wrong code to watch the dissolve.
interaction.touch: A numeric keyboard opens on tap and paste fills every cell at once.
